chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humid, who raised it (to the Imam), saying:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was asked about Divine Unity, so he said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, knew that there would be people in the Last Days who would think deeply

therefore, Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed: 'Say: He Allah is One. Allah is the Needless.' and the verses from the surah 'the Iron' - until He says: 'And He is Cognizant of what is in the hearts.'
Thus whosoever goes beyond that is ruined.

key_terms.ذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ: What is in the hearts (inner essence)

ai.seo_question: What is the boundary of Divine Unity according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) identifies Surah Al-Ikhlas and the concluding verses of Surah Al-Hadid as the sufficient boundaries for Tawhid, warning that excessive speculation (ta'til) beyond these revealed limits leads to spiritual ruin. This hadith underscores the Shia principle of limiting theological inquiry to what is explicitly revealed, preventing the complexities of divine attributes from obscuring the core message of Unity.
